encounters.cc: Progressive exertional dyspnea and chest discomfort

lines: Progressive exertional dyspnea and chest discomfort

The patient is a 69-year-old male with coronary artery disease status post myocardial infarction, rheumatic fever, and established care for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and peripheral arterial disease who presents for Cardiology evaluation.

He reports progressive exertional dyspnea and chest discomfort with uphill walking or stair climbing, along with occasional palpitations and mild fatigue, and denies orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and leg swelling.
- Coronary artery disease (status post myocardial infarction)
His medical history includes poorly controlled hypertension for many years and hyperlipidemia.
- Cardiac catheterization with percutaneous coronary intervention (prior)
He has a 25-pack-year smoking history and drinks alcohol socially.
Blood pressure is 168/96 mm Hg, pulse is 78/min, and BMI is 29 kg/m².
On exam, the apical impulse is sustained and laterally displaced.
First and second heart sounds are normal, with no murmurs or gallops.
Echocardiography reveals a thickened left ventricular wall with normal ejection fraction and no regional wall motion abnormalities.
ECG shows increased QRS voltage with prominent R waves in V5–V6 and T wave inversions in lateral leads.

encounters.cc: Worsening shortness of breath and frequent respiratory infections

lines: Worsening shortness of breath and frequent respiratory infections

The patient is a 71-year-old male with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and coronary artery disease status post myocardial infarction who returns to the Pulmonology clinic for continued management of respiratory symptoms, having previously presented with progressive dyspnea in 2022 and 2024.
He reports worsening shortness of breath, chronic productive cough, and frequent respiratory infections over the past two years.
He has been treated for two episodes of acute bronchitis in the past six months.
The patient expresses a desire to improve his health and is willing to consider lifestyle modifications.
- Hypertensive Heart Disease with End-Organ Damage (indication for echocardiography) (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
- Coronary artery disease (status post myocardial infarction)
- Cardiac catheterization with percutaneous coronary intervention (prior)
Oxygen saturation on room air is 92%
Prolonged expiratory phase with wheezing and decreased breath sounds at the lung bases
Chest X-ray reveals hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms.
Spirometry shows an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.65, which is minimally reversible with bronchodilators.
